alt: Background: the USSR was mainly a peasant country and peasants held back grain in 1927-28. Four aims of modernisation: defence against the capitalist powers, communist ideology, reliable grain for cities and exports, and Stalin's power.
caption: Defence, ideology, grain and power all pushed Stalin towards rapid change.

alt: Peasants' land, animals and tools are merged into a collective farm, which delivers fixed grain quotas to the state. A Machine Tractor Station supplies machinery and lets the party watch the villages; on state farms peasants worked for wages.
caption: Collective farms delivered fixed quotas to the state, watched through the tractor stations.

alt: Vertical timeline of collectivisation: the 1929 campaign and call to liquidate the kulaks, peasant resistance that halved livestock, "Dizzy with Success" in March 1930, the August 1932 law, the famine of 1932-33, internal passports, and near-total collectivisation by the end of the 1930s.
caption: Collectivisation was completed at the cost of famine and millions of deaths.

alt: Three linked cards for the Five-Year Plans: heavy industry (1928-32), heavy industry plus transport (1933-37) and rearmament (1938-41). Below, a bar chart of official steel output, about 4 million tonnes in 1928 and about 18 million in 1940, with a warning that figures may be exaggerated.
caption: Heavy industry grew fast, at least on paper; consumer goods were neglected.

after: ## Consequences for the groups named in the specification
alt: Table of gains and losses for kulaks, city dwellers, industrial workers, professional workers and women under Stalin's modernisation, from deportation of kulaks to new opportunities and a double burden for women.
caption: Modernisation brought opportunity to some groups and suffering to many.

alt: Two columns weighing the extent of modernisation: heavy industry, cities, education and eastern industry were transformed, but agriculture, consumer goods and housing lagged, and the costs in forced labour, terror and famine were enormous.
caption: Industry and defence modernised; the countryside and living standards did not.

alt: Two ways women were affected: new opportunities in paid work with crèches, and tighter state control of family life through the 1936 Family Code. Together these produced a double burden of work and motherhood.
caption: Work and family policy together created the double burden.
